## Historical audit: S0121

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C1/selection/commons_133800864/trajectory.jsonl`. This audit covers only supplied chunk 1 of 2; the reference and renders themselves are not visible here.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The explicit goal was an editable, separate-mesh reconstruction of one indoor photograph, matching camera, framing, materials and occlusion. The student’s initial comments interpret it as a kitchen corner; that interpretation is not independent image evidence. |
| Student response and execution, lines 3–5 | A nonempty SceneAct program built multiple grouped objects: window/blinds, cabinet, counter/sink, towel, paper roll, appliances, jug and pitcher. It specified a camera, area lights, colored materials and procedural counter texture. Components such as towel mount/ring/folds and pitcher handle were modeled separately; their actual contact and appearance are unverified. Step 1 reported `ok: true` and saved a render and blend file. |
| Student request and response, lines 8–11 | The student received the step-1 result and an attached render, then diagnosed framing as too wide and the towel as misplaced. The executed revision changed camera position and lens 51→65, moved and broadened the towel, darkened materials and adjusted lighting. These are student diagnoses and operations, not verified improvements. |
| Execution result and student response, lines 12–18 | Step 2 reported success and was selected. Given its render, the student diagnosed a narrow cabinet cheek, misplaced towel, pitcher position and counter texture. Step 3 deepened the cabinet, repositioned and broadened the towel, moved the pitcher, and explicitly assigned a procedural stone material; it also changed lighting and camera target. Angled blinds, cloth folds, blender cup and pitcher lid show modeled poses, not verified pose matches. |
| Execution result and selections, lines 19–21 | Step 3 reported `ok: true`, a finished 16-sample render and saved blend file; selection events recorded step 3. This establishes **technical build/render success**, not formal visual or geometric correctness. Final submission and overall outcome remain unknown in this chunk. |

**Input and autonomy.** The visible feedback was harness-provided execution status and a generic comparison instruction, with render attachments (lines 8 and 15); no separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-derived adoption is visible. The student independently produced the specific diagnoses and revisions. Sessions reported zero tool calls (lines 2, 9, 16); the three runner executions are separately recorded. No independent exploration beyond this render-and-revise loop is shown.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, a successful render is an execution check, while camera, material, connection and pose fidelity require visual or geometric comparison. Here, the repeated counter-texture and towel revisions are task-specific responses to student-claimed discrepancies. Whether texture assignment worked visually, parts truly meet, framing and lighting match, or any revision improved similarity remains unresolved. No technical interruption, empty patch, or algorithm failure is shown; neither partial visual correctness nor final formal success can be established without the unseen images or remaining chunk.
